title: Enjoy a Cozy and Green Bath

limitations: All 51 pages were rendered and visually reviewed; equation-heavy pages and the Report were inspected at full resolution.
OCR damages mathematical glyphs and some units, so rendered equations/tables are authoritative.
CFD settings, parameter provenance, duplicate water figures, and scenario uncertainty are incomplete.

task_reconstruction.source: Summary, Introduction, model overview, sub-models I/II, correction/contrast, sensitivity, Further Discussion, Strength/Weakness, and Report
deliverables: Compare continuous and discontinuous hot-water strategies using comfort and water-consumption criteria.
Correct ideal models for evaporation and assess radiation.
Analyze volume, shape, person, motion, bubble, and faucet-layout factors.
Recommend an implementable user strategy and explain spatial nonuniformity.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No separate official Problem A statement was located; the paper's explicit restatement and path-derived A classification are retained.

section_map.summary: Three criteria, two sub-models, correction, comparison, sensitivity, and recommendation.
Background, literature, problem restatement, and ordered work plan.
Continuous PDE, mean, capacity, parameters, and CFD.
Transient heating, standby cooling, cycle timing, and CFD.
Evaporation correction, criteria, water accounting, recommendation.
Volume, shape, person, bubbles, radiation, and faucet arrangement.
Positive scope and unresolved transfer risks.
Designed user recommendations and physical explanation.

contributions.summary: Coupled flow/energy PDE and composite heat-loss capacity for continuous addition.
Transient heating plus exponential standby cycle.
Mean temperature and water consumption comparison.
Geometry, person, motion, bubble, radiation, and faucet scenarios.
Five practical suggestions and mechanism explanation.

edges.handoff: CFD temperature field is reduced to mean temperature and energy capacity.
Mean-temperature energy accounting supplies composite boundary-loss capacity.
Continuous-model boundaries and properties are inherited by the transient heating model.
Heating ends at an upper threshold and enters standby cooling.
Cycle times and mass flows enter model comparison and recommendation.
Heat-capacity components are perturbed for geometry/person/material sensitivity.
CFD field and residual behavior support scenario and faucet-layout checks.
Scenario tables and spatial simulations become decision criteria and Report suggestions.

feedbacks: Sensitivity and faucet scenarios modify capacity, boundaries, or geometry, then return to the same comparison metrics and Report.

assumptions.summary: No internal source before person extension; stable inlet temperature.
Mesh and simulation reductions for tractability.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Tables 2-3 assign physical and geometry values.

models.summary: A rectangular bathwater domain uses incompressible-flow, momentum, and energy equations with inlet, free-surface, and wall boundary conditions.
The bath is treated as a constant-temperature system to derive average state and composite heat-transfer capacity.
The model expresses total heat-transfer capacity as a sum of surface fluxes, then treats evaporation as a later correction.
The intermittent model adds unsteady terms to momentum and energy equations and terminates heating at an upper mean-temperature threshold.
A control-volume energy balance yields exponential cooling, standby time, and total heat-transfer capacity.
Gambit mesh and Fluent steps produce residual curves and color temperature fields for full and reduced geometries.
The study perturbs one factor or a small scenario family, recalculates capacities and flows, then translates directions into bathtub advice.
Corrected tables compare average temperature, timing, mass flow, and water consumption; the Report translates the selected strategy into five practical suggestions.

verification.summary: Residual and mesh figures support solver execution/stability.
Color fields show local gradients and stable mean.
Humidity curve and energy conservation update loss capacity.
Radiative power is compared with total capacity.
Alternative entrance layouts are compared through field maps.

results_trace.summary: Mean temperature stable but field not strictly even.
Continuous addition recommended after corrected water comparison.
Table 18 compares ideal, evaporation, shape, static, moving, and bubble cases.
Five suggestions return results to users.

writing_logic.summary: the bathtub task and prior evidence | compress the whole route and recommendation | name criteria, sub-models, correction, comparison, sensitivity, and user handoff | a complete claim inventory | Introduction expands context and roadmap | scope -> models -> correction -> decision -> user artifact

everyday cooling and literature mechanisms | establish the gap and a staged work plan | define deliverables, assumptions, two sub-models, comparisons, sensitivity, application | the paper contract | Assumptions fixes the tractable regime | context -> literature -> task -> roadmap

the real-life bath system | bound physics and parameter treatment | state fluid, property, source, radiation, and inlet assumptions | a justified model scope | Notation binds symbols to units | assumption -> justification -> scope

the scope and symbols needed by later equations | make units and symbols stable | define h,k,cp,rho,delta,t,qm,Phi,T,V,M,A,a,b,c | a shared parameter vocabulary | Model Overview introduces architecture | symbols -> units -> model inputs

goals, notation, and rectangular bath geometry | derive continuous heating model and capacity | write PDE/boundaries, define mean, composite resistance, and parameters | continuous sub-model | Results computes and simulates it | goals -> PDE -> mean -> capacity -> CFD

continuous-model interfaces and cycle analogy | derive intermittent heating and standby | add unsteady flow/energy, control-volume energy, cooling ODE, and cycle thresholds | discontinuous sub-model | Results calibrates cycle values | heating -> energy handoff -> standby -> cycle

both sub-models and parameter tables | calculate and simulate outputs | substitute values, run CFD, interpret residuals and temperature fronts | model outputs and cycle recommendation | Correction audits omitted evaporation | parameters -> equations -> fields -> recommendation

parameterized equations and the simulation plan | turn the analytical model into an executable numerical workflow | mesh geometry, assign materials and boundaries, iterate residuals, and export field evidence | CFD residuals and temperature fields | Model Improvement reuses the numerical workflow for intermittent heating | equations -> mesh -> solver -> field evidence

ideal model outputs | correct omitted evaporation and compare alternatives | add empirical loss, define criteria, calculate water, and select continuous addition | corrected recommendation | Sensitivity tests factors | omission -> correction -> metrics -> decision

corrected sub-models and their decision metrics | test transfer across volume, shape, person, bubbles, radiation, and faucets | perturb, recompute, plot, explain mechanism, and advise | conditional design guidance | Further Discussion extends faucet layout and application | factor -> response -> mechanism -> advice

corrected scenarios | summarize the recommended operating strategy | rank scenarios by flow, time, and water consumption | decision matrix | Further Discussion turns it into implementation | scenario matrix -> policy

simulation evidence and ideal-model caveats | communicate practical application | recommend continuous flow, smaller tub, fewer motions, bubbles, and more faucets; explain unevenness | user report and implementation ideas | Strengths/Weaknesses bounds confidence | technical evidence -> user actions

full modeling chain | evaluate evidence and transfer limits | list thermodynamic basis, corrections, CFD, criteria, and parameter/motion gaps | bounded quality assessment | Report communicates selected guidance | strengths -> weaknesses -> confidence
the report | close provenance | list sources without adding reusable prose | citation boundary | end of paper | provenance -> close

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A separate, audience-specific report may aid judge auditability and communication; award status is not causal evidence.

weaknesses.summary: Source units and parameter provenance are incomplete.
Color values are expanded and software limitations are acknowledged.
Mass-flow and time values are difficult to reconcile across prose/table.
Continuous water totals are duplicated inconsistently.
Intermittent CFD uses short/reduced runs versus long analytic cycle.
Contact area is fixed and motion is represented by coefficient perturbation.
Application flow differs from some corrected table values.

independent_extensions.summary: Couple full three-dimensional Navier-Stokes/energy flow with validated geometry, mixing, and long-horizon time stepping.
Calibrate evaporation and radiation jointly with humidity/temperature measurements and propagate uncertainty.
Model person pose/contact area and motion as coupled uncertain inputs, then report robust strategy reversals.
Optimize faucet placement under manufacturing, pressure, and water-use constraints rather than comparing a few layouts.

unresolved_questions: What exact mesh, element/finite-volume scheme, time step, residual tolerance, and solver version were used?
Why do repeated tables/prose report different water totals and flows?
What are the units and sources for every thermal-resistance and evaporation parameter?
How are the continuous steady model and intermittent transient model jointly calibrated?
How does contact area vary with person volume/pose and motion?
What uncertainty and interaction structure supports the sensitivity recommendations?
Can the five Report suggestions be translated into a feedback controller with measured sensors?
